input.quote: a) MSL expressly warrants that all Products, MSL supplied materials and Parts, and work prepared for IBM will conform in all material respects to the specifications, drawings, or other descriptions furnished or adopted by IBM, and will be of specified quality, good workmanship, and free from defect subject to the following terms:
input.rationale: MSL gives an express conformance and workmanship warranty on all Products, materials, Parts and work prepared for IBM (§ 19.1(a)), with stated durations of [*] months for MSL Procured Parts (§ 19.1(a)(iv)) and [*] months for workmanship (§ 19.1(a)(v)), running from delivery, surviving acceptance testing and expressly covering latent defects (p1068). The remedy set matches the playbook: MSL must repair or replace defective Products and, where repair or replacement is not possible, refund MSL's price for the failed Product and Parts (§ 19.5). The § 19.6 disclaimer is limited to "ALL OTHER TERMS AND CONDITIONS" and expressly preserves "MSL'S WARRANTY OBLIGATIONS DESCRIBED IN THIS SECTION 19", so it does not swallow the express warranty, and the "AS IS" language at § 8.0(d) and the loaned-equipment terms run in our favour. This sits at (and on duration likely above) the fallback position — conformance warranty measured in months rather than 90 days, with repair, replacement and refund — so we do not redline it. Noted short of preferred only: there is no separate "professional and workmanlike" services standard beyond "good workmanship", no compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty, and the warranty periods are redacted ([*] months), which we would confirm commercially rather than flag. This is a hardware manufacturing engagement; the only software involved is IBM's own Software Packages installed by MSL under Attachment 6, so no MSL software-to-documentation warranty is expected.
